title: Pseudo-coherent derived evaluation isomorphism
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $K,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that $K$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], that $L$ is bounded below in the derived category, i.e. $L\in D^+(R)$, meaning $H^i(L)=0$ for all $i\ll0$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], and that $M$ has finite injective dimension (isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $R$-modules) [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the canonical derived evaluation morphism of [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map]
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L),M)$$
is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Choose a bounded-above complex $P$ of finite free $R$-modules representing $K$, by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and an integer $u$ with $P^s=0$ for $s>u$. The finite-injective-dimension hypothesis, in the explicit meaning given in the statement, supplies a bounded complex of injective modules $I$ representing $M$; fix $a\le b$ with $I^p=0$ outside $[a,b]$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives] the abelian category of $R$-modules has enough injectives. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] to $L\in D^+(R)$ to obtain a bounded-below complex of injectives $J$ representing $L$, with $J^j=0$ for $j<\ell$. Both $I$ and $J$ are K-injective by the bounded-below-injective assertion of that same node. All bounds are bounds on terms of these chosen complexes, not just on their cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0A68, proof, choices of representatives; derived.tex Tags 013K and 070J

proof.text: Each $P^s$ is flat: after choosing a finite basis, tensoring with $P^s$ is a finite direct sum of the identity functor on modules, and hence preserves exact sequences componentwise. Consequently [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat] makes $P$ K-flat. Use the equivalent quasi-isomorphism criterion of [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] to express this in the categorical K-flat convention. Then [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], together with the symmetry $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{|x||y|}y\otimes x$, computes $R\operatorname{Hom}(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ by $T=\operatorname{Tot}(H\otimes_R P)$, where $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(J,I)$. No K-flatness of $H$ is required.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; Tag 0A68, displayed total tensor model

proof.text: Specialize [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] to the one-object ringed site with ring $R$. Because $I,J$ are K-injective, it identifies $H=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(J,I)$ with a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(L,M)$, $A=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(P,J)$ with a representative of $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(K,L)$, and $B=\operatorname{Hom}_R^\bullet(A,I)$ with a representative of the target. These are the product total Hom complexes of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], with differential $d(f)=d_{\rm target}f-(-1)^{|f|}fd_{\rm source}$.

source.place: Tag 0A68, first displayed map of complexes; Tag 0A5W, section-RHom; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08J7

proof.text:
Fix a degree $n$. A potentially nonzero triple component is indexed by $p+r+s=n$ and has source $\operatorname{Hom}_R(J^{-r},I^p)\otimes_R P^s$. Necessarily $a\le p\le b$, $r\le-\ell$, and $s\le u$, whence $n-b+\ell\le s\le u$ and $n-b-u\le r\le-\ell$. Thus there are finitely many such triples. Moreover $A^k=\prod_s\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,J^{s+k})$ has only $\ell-k\le s\le u$ potentially nonzero factors. Hence every product that occurs here is a finite product after zero factors are removed, and so equals the finite direct sum. Using the component projections and inclusions gives the identifications
$$T^n\cong\bigoplus_{p+r+s=n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(J^{-r},I^p)\otimes_R P^s,$$
$$B^n\cong\bigoplus_{p+r+s=n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,J^{-r}),I^p),$$
with the finite ranges just proved. The identifications use only finite distributivity of tensor over sums and the fact that a linear map from a finite direct sum is the tuple of its restrictions.

source.place: Tag 0A68, proof, component description and final finite-support argument

proof.text:
Define $E:T\to B$ on the triple summand $(p,r,s)$ to be
$$g\otimes x\longmapsto\bigl(f\longmapsto\epsilon_{p,r,s}\,g(f(x))\bigr),\qquad\epsilon_{p,r,s}=(-1)^{s(r+1)},$$
where $g:J^{-r}\to I^p$, $x\in P^s$, and $f:P^s\to J^{-r}$. Extend by the finite sum in Step 4 and by precomposing with the corresponding projection of $A^{p-n}$. This is a chain map. Indeed, substituting the Hom differential and total tensor differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], equality for the terms involving $d_I,d_J,d_P$, respectively, reduces to
$$\epsilon_{p,r,s}=\epsilon_{p+1,r,s},\qquad\epsilon_{p,r,s}=(-1)^s\epsilon_{p,r-1,s},\qquad\epsilon_{p,r,s+1}=(-1)^{r+1}\epsilon_{p,r,s}.$$
All three follow immediately from the displayed exponent. Thus there is no unverified assertion about compatibility with differentials.

source.place: Tag 0A60, lemma-evaluate-and-more, equations alpha and beta and the three sign recurrences

proof.text: The localized $E$ is the specified canonical evaluation, rather than an arbitrary map between the two objects. To check this, transpose as in [lem-trf-derived-evaluation-canonical-map]. Write $h=p+r$, $k=-r-s$, so $g$ has Hom degree $h$ and $f$ has Hom degree $k$. In the composite $A\otimes H\otimes P\to I$, moving $f$ past $g$ contributes $(-1)^{kh}$; the two evaluations then give $g(f(x))$. The ordinary Hom transposition from $A\otimes T$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(A,I)$ contributes $(-1)^{kn}$, where $n=h+s$. Thus the adjoint sends $g\otimes x$ to $f\mapsto(-1)^{k(h+n)}g(f(x))=(-1)^{ks}g(f(x))$. Since $ks=(-r-s)s\equiv s(r+1)\pmod2$, this is exactly Step 5. Here evaluation with the Hom factor first is $f\otimes x\mapsto f(x)$, as follows directly from the Hom differential. Choose a K-flat resolution of $A$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object site. These computations also hold after precomposing $A$ with that resolution: both sides simply replace $f$ by its image in $A$. Since $P$ is K-flat and $I,J$ are K-injective, the tensor and Hom models in Steps 2 and 3 compute precisely these derived composites and their transpose. This verifies the canonical normalization, including its sign, on the chosen models.

source.place: Tags 0A67 and 0A61, lemma-internal-hom-evaluate and remark-sign-explanation, direct transposition computation

proof.text: For each triple, put $V=J^{-r}$ and $W=I^p$. The unsigned map $c:\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,W)\otimes_R P^s\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,V),W)$, $c(g\otimes x)(f)=g(f(x))$, is an isomorphism by the following explicit finite-basis argument. Choose a finite basis $(e_i)$ of $P^s$ and let $\iota_i:V\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P^s,V)$ send $v$ to the map taking $e_j$ to $\delta_{ij}v$. The inverse sends $\beta$ to $\sum_i(\beta\circ\iota_i)\otimes e_i$. Composing with $c$ gives $f\mapsto\sum_i\beta(\iota_i(f(e_i)))=\beta(f)$. Conversely, on $g\otimes x$, writing $x=\sum_i x_i e_i$ gives $\sum_i x_i g\otimes e_i=g\otimes x$. Thus both composites are identities. Multiplying $c$ by the unit $\epsilon_{p,r,s}\in\{1,-1\}$ preserves invertibility. Step 4 identifies $E^n$ with a finite direct sum of these invertible maps, so $E^n$ is invertible for every integer $n$.

source.place: Tag 0A68, proof, maps c_{p,r,s}; finite-free specialization with the inverse written explicitly

proof.text: The componentwise inverses of $E$ form a chain map: from $d_BE=Ed_T$, multiply in consecutive degrees by the two component inverses to obtain $E^{-1}d_B=d_TE^{-1}$. Hence $E$ is an isomorphism of complexes. Localization into $D(R)$ preserves its inverse by functoriality [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. With the identifications of Steps 2 and 3 and the normalization of Step 6, its localization is exactly the canonical morphism in the statement. It is therefore an isomorphism.
